correctness.rationale: For the alternating determinant bracket [x,y,z]=det(x,y,z)e1, the Reynolds defect is a map on Λ^3(K^3) and hence completely determined by (e1,e2,e3), including in characteristics 2 and 3. Its first three mixed determinants sum to sigma2(R), and the all-R determinant is D, giving D e1=(sigma2-D) R(e1). Writing s=sigma2-D produces D=sa, sd=sg=0 and yields precisely the three disjoint cases: first column zero; nonpreserving first column with D=sigma2=0; nonzero scalar first column and det B=tr B. The first case has q^6 points; the third (q-1)q^2|SL2(Fq)|=q^3(q-1)(q^2-1). In the middle case Z={D=sigma2=0}, trace-zero nilpotent classes total q^6, nonzero trace t classes total q^4(q^2+q+1) each, so |Z|=q^7+q^6-q^4. Its first-line-preserving subset has 2q^5-q^3 points, yielding q^7+q^6-2q^5-q^4+q^3 for the genuine middle case. Rank<=1 matrices all satisfy D=sigma2=0; the exact rank-one number is (q^3-1)^2/(q-1). Invertible cases require B-I∈SL2 with tr(B-I)≠-2; exactly q^2 matrices in SL2 have trace -2 for every characteristic, giving q^3(q-1)(q^2-q-1). Rank two is subtraction. Independent SymPy reconstruction verifies the mixed-determinant sigma2 identity and polynomial sum. Exhaustive independent GF(4)=F2[u]/(u²+u+1) count (1,1323,21780,2112) matches the polynomial profile; package directly exhausts F2/F3 and matches (1,49,150,8), (1,338,2928,270). A count polynomial over every F_{q^m} gives the stated Hasse--Weil zeta factors by the exponential definition. Finite tests corroborate and do not establish the general proof.

value.rationale: The bracket [e1,e2,e3]=e1 is the natural nontrivial three-dimensional 3-Lie model used in the primary Reynolds/Nijenhuis literature. The full singular plus invertible Reynolds locus, not just the derivation-correspondence open subset, is a meaningful structural classification. Its characteristic-free three-case description and exact q-dependent rank profile for every finite field are natural intrinsic benchmark invariants; the same formula determines all extension-field counts and a nontrivial zeta rational function. These facts are not in the inspected general abstract Reynolds theory and are not merely a tiny numerical sample. The calculation does use elementary determinants and standard matrix similarity classes, but it solves a complete finite-dimensional operator variety with mathematically motivated domain. No quotient by 3-Lie automorphisms or classification of arbitrary 3-Lie algebras is claimed.
residual_risks: Scope is one fixed three-dimensional algebra, not a classification of all small n-Lie algebras.
Some matrix-class counting ingredients are routine; mathematical value lies in their complete combined Reynolds classification and field-uniform arithmetic.

limitations: Fixed algebra [e1,e2,e3]=e1 in dimension 3, over all fields; finite-field polynomial is for all prime-power q.
No classification of other 3-Lie algebras and no automorphism-conjugacy orbit quotient.
